findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes every workflow reminder, not just SMS
findings.body: The new deleteMany OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 and does not constrain method, scheduled, or scheduledDate. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP. This SMS cron therefore deletes other channels' rows (and already-scheduled SMS rows) as soon as retryCount exceeds 1, even if those reminders are still valid and were never handled by this job. That silently drops reminders the cron should not own.

findings.title: Missing phone or empty message never increments retryCount
findings.body: retryCount is only incremented inside `if (message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` or in the catch around that block. If sendTo is missing/empty (the invalid-or-absent phone case this PR is meant to stop) or the rendered message is empty, the reminder is neither scheduled nor counted as a failure, and the earlier `continue` when workflowStep or booking is missing has the same gap. Those rows stay scheduled=false with retryCount 0 and are selected again on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past, so the infinite reschedule loop remains for the failure mode described in the PR.

findings.title: retryCount update is a lost-update read-modify-write
findings.body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the value read at the start of the loop (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic increment. Overlapping cron invocations can both read the same count and write the same next value, so failures are under-counted and the retryCount > 1 delete never trips. The reminder then keeps being rescheduled indefinitely, which is the bug this change is supposed to fix. Use Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` so concurrent runs cannot collapse retries.
